Europe|website=www.fibaeurope.com|access-date=2018-04-15}} At {{Height|ft=6|in=3}}, {{Convert|175|lb}}, Douby played [[shooting guard]] for the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball statistical leaders|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]. The [[Sacramento Kings]] made him the 19th selection of the [[2006 NBA draft]]. ==High school career== Douby grew up in the [[Coney Island]] neighborhood of [[Brooklyn]].{{cite news|last=Breslauer|first=Danny|title=Quincy Douby: From Coney Island to Piscataway to the Sacramento Kings|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/37292-quincy-douby-from-coney-island-to-piscataway-to-the-sacramento-kings|access-date=26 February 2016|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=July 13, 2008}} He attended the nearby [[William E. Grady CTE High School|William E. Grady High School]], playing for the basketball team his junior and senior years, after he was discovered playing pick up basketball by New York City Hall of Fame coach Jack Ringel. Ringel helped develop Douby's raw skills and athleticism and transform his as player. During his junior season, Grady won the [[Public Schools Athletic League|PSAL]] A division championship, with Douby scoring 19 points in the championship game after Grady rode him the whole season.{{cite news|last1=Ackert|first1=Kristie|last2=Brennan|first2=Sean|title=GRADY FOLLOWS DOUBY LEAD TO BROOKLYN TITLE|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/grady-douby-lead-brooklyn-title-article-1.900006|access-date=26 February 2016|work=[[Daily News (New York)]]|date=January 18, 2001}} In his senior year, Douby averaged 35.6 points per game, leading Grady to the PSAL semifinals. Douby set the school record by scoring 63 points in an all-around performance against [[Franklin Delano Roosevelt High School (New York City)|Franklin D. Roosevelt High School]].{{cite news|last=Ackert|first=Kristie|title=DOUBY POURS IN GRADY-RECORD 63 POINTS|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/douby-pours-grady-record-63-points-article-1.932107|access-date=26 February 2016|work=[[Daily News (New York)]]|date=December 20, 2001}} Douby then enrolled in the [[St. Thomas More School (Connecticut)|St. Thomas More School]] [[University-preparatory school|prep school]] in [[Oakdale, Connecticut]] for the 2002–03 year.{{cite news|title=Quincy Douby Commits to Scarlet Knights|url=http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/120902aaa.html|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]|date=December 9, 2002|location=[[Piscataway, New Jersey]]|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428142118/http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/120902aaa.html|url-status=dead}} Douby initially committed to [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra University]] to play basketball, until head coach of [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball statistical leaders|Rutgers University]] men's basketball team, Gary Waters jumped in and swayed Douby to commit to the Scarlet Knights.{{cite news|last=Martin|first=Dan|title=DOUBY PICKS RUTGERS|url=https://nypost.com/2002/09/05/douby-picks-rutgers/|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[New York Post]]|date=September 5, 2002}} Douby was able to make the transformation from a street baller, to a [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] basketball player. Due to his close relationship with high school coach Jack Ringel, Douby would purchase a house in Ringel's neighboring town of [[Freehold Township, New Jersey|Freehold]], [[New Jersey]]. ==College career== As a freshman at Rutgers, Douby scored 35 points to lead the team to an overtime victory in the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] semifinal game.{{cite news|last=Ackert|first=Kristie|title=KNIGHTS HANG ON DOUBY'S 35 LIFT RUTGERS IN OT|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/archives/sports/knights-hang-douby-35-lift-rutgers-ot-article-1.552238|access-date=26 February 2016|work=[[Daily News (New York)]]|date=March 31, 2004}} Douby was named to the [[Big East]] All-Rookie Team at the end of his freshman year.{{cite news|title=OKAFOR AND GORDON HEADLINE ALL-BIG EAST FIRST TEAM; BOONE, T. BROWN & VILLANUEVA ALSO HONORED|url=http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030804aaa.html|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[Connecticut Huskies]]|date=March 8, 2004|location=[[Providence, Rhode Island]]|archive-date=May 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160507061939/http://www.uconnhuskies.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030804aaa.html|url-status=dead}} Douby improved on his freshman season by averaging 15.1 points a game (11th in the Big East) and 3.38 assists a game, while posting an assist-to-turnover ratio of 2:1. He was named Big East player of the Week along with [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]]'s Tyrone Sally the week of November 29.{{cite news|title=Bailey, Douby Receive BIG EAST Weekly Honors|url=http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112904aaa.html|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]|date=November 29, 2004|location=[[Piscataway, New Jersey]]|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428132741/http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/112904aaa.html|url-status=dead}} Despite finishing last in the Big East, Rutgers upset [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] in the first round of the Big East Tournament, with Douby scoring 15 points in the game.{{cite news|title=Rutgers Upsets Notre Dame in BIG EAST First Round 72–65|url=http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030905aaa.html|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]|date=March 9, 2005|location=[[New York City|New York]], [[New York (state)|New York]]|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428132400/http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030905aaa.html|url-status=dead}} In his junior year, Douby, as guard, was named to the All-Big East team.{{cite news|title=Douby Named First-Team All-BIG EAST|url=http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030606aaa.html|access-date=24 April 2016|work=[[Rutgers Scarlet Knights]]|date=March 6, 2006|location=[[Piscataway, New Jersey]]|archive-date=April 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160428160834/http://www.scarletknights.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030606aaa.html|url-status=dead}} He led the Big East in scoring with 25.4 points a game, becoming the first Rutgers player to lead the Big East in scoring. In addition, he broke the all-time single-season scoring record at Rutgers. Douby scored a Big East season high and [[Carrier Dome]] opponent record 41 points at [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]] on February 1, 2006. After leading Rutgers to a first-round victory in the Big East tournament over [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]], Douby dropped 31 over the #2 [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova Wildcats]]. On May 15, 2006, Douby officially hired an agent making himself ineligible to return to college. ==Professional career== On June 28, 2006, Douby was drafted in the first round by the Sacramento Kings, 19th overall. Douby became the first Rutgers player to be drafted in the first round since [[Roy Hinson]] in 1983. On July 3, 2006, he was signed to a contract by Sacramento. On February 18, 2009, Douby was waived by the Kings in order make room for the trade that included [[Brad Miller (basketball)|Brad Miller]] and [[Drew Gooden (basketball)|Drew Gooden]].{{cite web |last=Hollis |first=L. |date=February 17, 2009 |title=Sacramento Kings Press Release - 0209 |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings_press_release0209.html |access-date=May 26, 2023 |work=NBA.com}} On March 11, 2009, Douby was picked up by the [[Osceola Magic|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/quincy_douby_031109.html |title=BayHawks Add Quincy Douby to Roster |work=NBA.com |date=March 11, 2009 |access-date=March 2, 2013}} On March 24, 2009, he was called up by the [[Toronto Raptors]] and signed to a 10-day contract.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/douby_090324.html Erie's Quincy Douby Called Up To Toronto Raptors] On April 3, he was signed to a second 10-day contract,[http://www.nba.com/2009/news/04/03/raptors.douby.ap/index.html Raptors sign G Douby to 10-day contract] which was extended up until the end of the [[2008–09 NBA season]] ten days later.[http://www.nba.com/2009/news/04/13/raptors.douby.ap/index.html Raptors sign guard Quincy Douby for next season] On November 12, 2009, Douby was released by the Raptors. He did not appear in any games for them during the [[2009–10 NBA season]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/news/douby_release_111209.html |title=Raptors Release Guard Quincy Douby |work=NBA.com |date=2009-11-12 |access-date=2009-11-12}} On November 17, 2009, Douby signed a one-year contract with the Turkish team [[Darüşşafaka Cooper Tires]].[http://www.tbf.org.tr/tbfweb/tbfweb2.nsf/($$TBFV1_BasinBulteni_TBL_WEB_View)/E5B3DA2C980245E5C2257671002F7F64?OpenDocument Reinforcement Cooper Tires'a Darussafaka NBA] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091118215821/http://www.tbf.org.tr/tbfweb/tbfweb2.nsf/($$TBFV1_BasinBulteni_TBL_WEB_View)/E5B3DA2C980245E5C2257671002F7F64?OpenDocument |date=November 18, 2009 }} He finished as the top scorer of the [[Turkish Basketball League]], averaging 23.6 points and 4.9 assists per game for his team. On September 17, 2010, Douby signed a one-year contract with the Chinese team [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]]. In March 2012 he signed with [[CB Murcia|UCAM Murcia]] until the end of the season.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/spain/36519/ucam-murcia-tabs-quincy-douby.html UCAM Murcia tabs Quincy Douby] Later that year, he returned to China as a member of the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]].[http://www.niubball.com/2012/06/quincy-douby-returns-to-china-signs-with-zhejiang/ Quincy Douby returns to China, signs with Zhejiang] On January 2, 2013, Douby set a CBA record for points with 75.[http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/01/02/quincy-douby-scored-75-in-chinese-league-game-video/ Quincy Douby scored 75 in Chinese league game] During the 2012–13 season, he averaged 31.6 points per game. Douby previously set CBA records for the most points scored in a Finals game (53) and in an All-Star game (44). At the end of the CBA season, he joined [[Sagesse Beirut]] in Lebanon.[http://basketball.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/Sagesse_lands_Quincy_Douby/314065 Sagesse lands Quincy Douby....] In September 2013, he played for [[Applied Science University (basketball team)|Applied Science University]] at the [[2013 FIBA Asia Champions Cup]].{{cite news|title=Quincy Douby to join ASU for Asia Champions Cup|url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Jordan/basketball.aspx?NewsID=330754|access-date=2 October 2013|work=Eurobasket.com|date=28 August 2013}} On November 1, 2013, he was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. Later that month, he left the Skyforce after just two games and signed with the Shanghai Sharks of China.[http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/230829/Quincy-Douby-Reaches-Deal-With-Shanghai-Sharks-Of-China Quincy Douby Reaches Deal With Shanghai Sharks Of China][http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/108501/quincy-douby-will-play-in-china.html Quincy Douby will play in China] On February 28, 2014, he signed with [[Darüşşafaka Basketbol|Darüşşafaka & Doğuş]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Second League]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/112411/quincy-douby-goes-to-tb2l-and-signs-with-darussafaka.html Quincy Douby goes to TB2L and signs with Darussafaka] In July 2014, he returned to China and signed with [[Tianjin Ronggang]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/129415/quincy-douby-signs-with-tianjin-steel.html Quincy Douby signs with TianJin Steel] On November 18, 2016, Douby was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the NBA D-League.{{cite web|first=Katie|last=Hatch|title=WESTCHESTER KNICKS ACQUIRE DOUBY, WAIVE KROMAH|url=http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-douby-waive-kromah/|work=NBA.com|date=November 18, 2016|access-date=November 21, 2016|archive-date=November 22, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161122000251/http://westchester.dleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-douby-waive-kromah/|url-status=dead}} On December 12, he early terminated his contract with the Knicks after appearing in two games.{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/|title=NBA D-League Transactions|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 14, 2016|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161213135838/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/|archive-date=December 13, 2016}} On January 5, 2017, he signed with Turkish club [[Afyonkarahisar Belediyespor]] for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Quincy Douby signs with Afyon Belediye|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/222248/quincy-douby-signs-with-afyon-belediye.html|access-date=January 5, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=January 5, 2017}} In August 2017, he signed with [[Sporting Al Riyadi Beirut]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]].[http://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/504922/Al-Riyadi-tabs-Quincy-Douby,-ex-Afyon Al Riyadi tabs Quincy Douby, ex
